title: Open reduction towers and the strict augmented tensor square
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On each small pro-etale site put $B_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and use the ordinary unbounded module derived category $D(B_W)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Open extension and restriction mean exact ringed-slice functors $e_!\dashv e^*$, applied termwise [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact].
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-open-immersion], and let $K\in D^b_c(U,R)$ and $P\in D^b_c(X,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. For $H\in D(B_W)$ write $H_n=H\otimes^L_{B_W}(A_n)_W$ and $Q_W(H)_\bullet=(\operatorname{Res}_n H_n)_n$, with the strict quotient transitions; $\operatorname{Res}_n$ forgets to $B_W$-modules along $B_W\to(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. Use flat-term K-flat representatives [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, lem-pc-kflat-resolution], the total right derived inverse limit on strict towers, and its normalized Roos model and augmentation comparison [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit].
Write $j_!^{A_n}$ for finite-coefficient extension and $J$ for its simultaneous strict-system version. There is a canonical isomorphism $r_\bullet:Q_X(j_!K)_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}JQ_U(K)_\bullet$ of derived strict systems, whose $n$-th component is the $A_n$-linear open scalar comparison
$$r_n:(j_!K)_n\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!^{A_n}K_n.$$
Its inverse is the open-unit transpose for $B_X\to(A_n)_X$ [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization, def-sf-open-reduction-coefficient-mate]; $r_\bullet$ is the comparison $r_j(K)$ of [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison]. Scalar restriction commutes with these open extensions and all quotient transitions. Both $j_!K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ and $j^*P\in D^b_c(U,R)$. Moreover $\mathcal H^q(j_!^{A_n}K_n)=j_!^{A_n}\mathcal H^q(K_n)$; every cohomological interval for $K_n$ also works for $j_!^{A_n}K_n$, uniformly in $n$ [lem-sf-open-finite-constructibility-interval]. A finite locally closed constructible partition for a cohomology sheaf on $U$ extends to one on $X$ by adding the reduced closed complement with zero module; restriction intersects a partition with $U$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. No finite-Tor hypothesis is imposed.
Set $H=j_!K\otimes^L_{B_X}P$, $H_U=K\otimes^L_{B_U}j^*P$ and use the inverse-open-unit-transpose isomorphism $\gamma^B:H\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!H_U$ [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Put
$$T_\bullet=\bigl(\operatorname{Res}_n((j_!K)_n\otimes^L_{(A_n)_X}P_n)\bigr)_n,\quad S_\bullet=\bigl(\operatorname{Res}_n(K_n\otimes^L_{(A_n)_U}j^*P_n)\bigr)_n.$$
Let $c_T:\Delta H\to T_\bullet$ and $c_S:\Delta H_U\to S_\bullet$ be the strict tensor quotient augmentations on these representatives [def-sf-tensor-completion-comparison]; $\Delta$ is the constant-tower functor. Through $r_\bullet$ and tensor change of rings [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], reduction of $\gamma^B$ is the simultaneous finite open tensor isomorphism $\gamma_\bullet:T_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}JS_\bullet$, and
$$\gamma_\bullet\circ c_T=J(c_S)\circ\Delta(\gamma^B).$$
This equality holds for the simultaneous augmented strict complex-system maps, hence in their derived category. Under balanced tensor identifications the coefficient-change map is $(x\otimes y)\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes1)$, preserving homogeneous degrees, signs and every quotient transition. In particular the equality includes the strict augmentation, rather than only its finite derived evaluations.

proof.text: Finite type over the field makes X and U Noetherian, hence j quasi-compact. The cardinality of the finite base field gives characteristic p. The distinct prime ell is a unit there and hence in global sections on X and U and all their stalks. Choose the existing compatible completed-open-tensor context; it supplies all calculus, coherence, ordinary and complete comparison witnesses simultaneously, including their agreement on complete inputs.

Apply openQuotientModelGeometry to this same context for the finite extension identification and both integral constructibility and interval assertions. For a constructible input K, its definition supplies constructibility of the nth reduction; apply the existing finite open interval theorem to that reduction and the supplied interval to prove FiniteGeometry, retaining its cohomology, stratum and stalk clauses. Convert a finite locally closed partition plus its supplied constructibility witnesses to the existing scheme Stratification, pull it back along j, and forget only its bundled constructibility field. The identity on indices and the actual pullback projections prove RestrictionPartitions.

Apply openQuotientNormalizedCochains to the same context for the tensor presentations, strict scalar comparison and normalized strict squares. Fill the unchanged Comparison structure with these witnesses and the preceding geometric facts. Its completeAgreement is the symmetry of the context sameOpen field. Package the context calculus and open-operation witnesses in the existential conclusion.

split_report.summary: Repair of the 7359-character proof: extracted two independent ordinary ringed-site cochain equations as statement-only unsplit tasks, with their generator values, signs, strict transitions and scalar-unit normalizations. Reused the already-existing general cochain balancing and K-flat total-tensor lemmas rather than creating duplicates. The unchanged statement is assembled in four short steps. The report preserves all seven old arguments verbatim and records their destinations.

tool_uses.why: Generic existence of flat-term K-flat representatives, needed to compute the stipulated strict quotient towers.
Generic immersion restriction preserving quotient completeness and the integral constructible category, needed for j^*P; no own-unit lemma supplies this domain fact.
Generic actual open reduction comparison and completeness preservation; needed to identify our strict map with r_j(K), which is explicitly named by the item.
Generic finite-stage constructibility and cohomology interval preservation, applied separately at every quotient; the own unit does not prove this finiteness input.
Generic unbounded open tensor chain model and simultaneous coefficient reduction formula; this supplies the computational input, not the tensor augmentation square proved here.
Generic arbitrary-coefficient open tensor isomorphism with the inverse-open-unit-transpose normalization, including the diagram-site version; fixes the map used throughout this unit.
Generic arbitrary-ringed-topos scalar pullback preserving K-flat representatives and its tensor comparison, applied only to the coefficient ring maps and open restriction.
Generic identity-on-extension-summands scalar restriction and strict coefficient comparison; used to retain the coefficient-linear normalization before forgetting scalars.
Generic unbounded sheaf-complex tensor K-flatness and flat terms, used only to compute another derived reduction.
Generic ringed-topos cochain tensor comparison with its explicit balanced inverse, signed differentials and strict coefficient-transition equations; no own-unit node supplies this chain calculation.

The item statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to the live node, which Q142 split and reviewed. The new proof is 4 assembly steps, 2179 chars in all, and proof_deps equals the union of step uses. No cycle, no route-pivot-dropped or merged id, no SGA. Where each old step went: steps 1, 2 and 4 were already assemblies of existing nodes and stay as citations. Step 1 now proves j quasi-compact before step 2 uses it, which fixes the forward reference noted by Q142. Old step 3 is carried by the kappa/eta statement of lem-sf-cbc-slice-tensor-generator-coherence. Old step 5 is carried by lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model and lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence, taking u = identity topos and coefficient map B->A_n. That node's c_u and its stated inverse are the balancing maps, and they commute with quotient transitions. Old steps 6 and 7 became the two new statement-only nodes. Node coefficient-interchange: checked by hand on generators. Both sides send ([x]⊗y)⊗a to [(x⊗j^*a)⊗(j^*y⊗1)], all types match, nothing is permuted, signs hold for odd x, and q_{m,n} sits in the same slot on both sides. Node scalar-unit-augmentation: both routes give [(x⊗1)⊗(j^*y⊗1)]. It is close to a corollary of node 1 plus the scalar-unit clause, but the two are statement-only generator tasks of the same size, each matching one old step. Neither restates the item. Sources read: Stacks 0E8I (sites-modules.tex:4051) and 0GL1 (sites-cohomology.tex:4578), and the open-factor paragraph of the main-20261015 blueprint. Edge cases: V empty, j = id, Q or F zero, A_n = 0, non-surjective towers. Duplicate candidates read: lem-coef-etale-open-scalar-coherence, lem-fix-open-scalar-tensor-normalization, lem-sp-canonical-open-scalar-tensor-models and lem-pur-kflat-open-projection-model.
